decisive_items: a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region
Although tumor markers were normal, the imaging findings were concerning for an ovarian neoplasm.
response.rationale: The vignette centers on a large right adnexal mass with imaging features suspicious for an ovarian neoplasm despite normal tumor markers. R4 directly matches this. R9 overstates malignancy without definitive evidence; R1 lacks specific fibroma features; R2 requires ascites not present; R5 is incidental; R6/R7/R8 address lymphedema but not the primary mass.

rejected.why: No ascites or pleural effusion described; Meigs syndrome requires these.
No specific imaging or histologic features of fibroma; solid-cystic lesion not typical.
Uterine fibroids are incidental and do not explain the adnexal mass.
Lymphedema is lifelong but not linked to the pelvic mass; no lymphatic malformation imaging.
Lymphedema is a sign, not the primary diagnosis; pelvic mass unexplained.
No vascular malformations or limb hypertrophy; only edema.
Malignancy is provisional; normal tumor markers and well-marginated lesion do not confirm malignancy.
